candidate_relations.reason: Hypotension and bradycardia on arrival are cardiovascular manifestations of amitraz, not the poisoning diagnosis itself.
Obtundation, hypercapnia, and intubation reflect respiratory depression from amitraz, not a separate diagnosis.
Miosis and atropine-responsive bradycardia mimic a cholinergic crisis, but documented 12.5% amitraz ingestion is an alpha-2 agonist toxidrome, not acetylcholinesterase inhibition.
Cholinergic syndrome is the organophosphate-like mimic; the history is amitraz solution ingestion rather than a cholinergic agent.
Pulse of 59 beats/min is a cardinal amitraz sign, not the etiologic diagnosis.
Cholinergic toxicity is a related toxidrome differential and does not name the ingested amitraz.
Organophosphate poisoning is the main clinical mimic given pinpoint pupils and bradycardia, but the alleged ingestant is amitraz, not an organophosphate.
Atropine-responsive bradycardia is a treated manifestation of amitraz, not the poisoning entity.
Amitraz poisoning is the same diagnostic object as the reference after witnessed amitraz ingestion.
Tachycardia after 0.6 mg atropine is an expected treatment effect, not atropine poisoning.
Acute respiratory acidosis (pH 7.24, PCO2 65 mmHg) is the blood-gas consequence of hypoventilation, not the toxicologic diagnosis.
Amitraz toxicity is a wording variant of amitraz poisoning for this ingestion.
